report:
# Is "Opening a Window/Door Improves Sleep Quality" False? Research Findings

The claim is **not simply false—it's conditionally true**. Evidence suggests opening a bedroom window or door can improve sleep, but only under favorable environmental conditions, and it can backfire otherwise.

**Supporting evidence:** A DTU (Technical University of Denmark) field study of 29 bedrooms found that opening windows or doors reduced CO2 buildup, and when ventilation kept CO2 below ~750 ppm, air quality was good enough that it didn't hinder sleep—researchers linked better bedroom ventilation to improved next-day cognitive performance (https://www.dtu.dk/english/newsarchive/2023/05/ventilate-your-bedroom-at-night-you-perform-better-the-next-day). A related study reported 87% of participants slept soundly with windows open vs. 70% with them closed (https://jewishreview.co.il/this-summer-trick-will-ensure-you-sleep-well-and-wake-up-refreshed-22702/).

**Contradicting evidence:** A Shanghai study of 50 residents found that while open windows improved air quality, sleep quality still suffered—likely due to summer heat and noise entering through open windows (https://www.sleepfoundation.org/sleep-news/open-window-may-be-better-for-sleep-but-we-keep-it-closed). Similarly, a follow-up DTU-affiliated study found that opening windows during summer nights actually *decreased* sleep quality, plausibly due to higher indoor temperature, PM2.5 pollution, and noise—despite improved ventilation rates (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S036013232301051X).

**Conclusion:** The claim holds true primarily when outdoor conditions are favorable (clean air, low noise, moderate temperature). Ventilation itself benefits sleep by reducing CO2, but opening a window is just one (often noisy, temperature-disrupting) method of achieving that ventilation. In poor outdoor conditions—heat, pollution, or noise—opening a window can worsen sleep despite better air exchange. The claim is best characterized as **context-dependent, not categorically false**.
